pois.name: Stanley Park
pois.intro: Stanley Park is a 405-hectare public park in British Columbia, Canada, that makes up the northwestern half of Vancouver's Downtown peninsula, surrounded by waters of Burrard Inlet and English Bay The park borders the neighbourhoods of West End and Coal Harbour to its southeast, and is connected to the North Shore via the Lions Gate Bridge.

pois.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
pois.intro: The Vancouver Art Gallery is an art museum in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The museum occupies a 15,300-square-metre-building adjacent to Robson Square in downtown Vancouver, making it the largest art museum in Western Canada by building size.

pois.name: Lions Gate Bridge
pois.intro: The Lions Gate Bridge, opened in 1938 and officially known as the First Narrows Bridge, is a suspension bridge that crosses the first narrows of Burrard Inlet and connects the City of Vancouver, British Columbia, to the North Shore municipalities of the District of North Vancouver, the City of North Vancouver, and West Vancouver.

pois.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
pois.intro: The Capilano Suspension Bridge is a simple suspension bridge crossing the Capilano River in Upper Capilano, British Columbia, Canada, in the District of North Vancouver. The current bridge is 140 metres long and 70 metres above the river.

pois.name: Waterfront Station
pois.intro: Waterfront station is a major intermodal public transportation facility and the main transit terminus in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is on West Cordova Street in Downtown Vancouver, between Granville and Seymour Street.

pois.name: False Creek
pois.intro: False Creek is a short narrow inlet in the heart of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, which separates the Downtown and West End neighbourhoods from the rest of the city. It is one of the four main bodies of water bordering Vancouver, along with English Bay, Burrard Inlet, and the Fraser River.

pois.name: Canada Place
pois.intro: Canada Place is a building situated on the Burrard Inlet in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is home to the Vancouver Convention Centre East Building, the Pan Pacific Vancouver Hotel, the Vancouver World Trade Centre, and the virtual flight experience Flyover in Vancouver.

pois.name: Harbour Centre
pois.intro: Harbour Centre is a skyscraper in the central business district of Downtown Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, which opened in 1977. The "Lookout" tower atop the office building makes it one of the tallest structures in Vancouver and a prominent landmark on the city's skyline.

pois.name: English Bay Beach
pois.intro: English Bay is an open bay northwest of the Burrard Peninsula in British Columbia, Canada, extending from the headland between Siwash Rock and Prospect Point on Vancouver's Downtown peninsula in the northeast, to the northwestern tip of Point Grey in the southwest.

pois.name: Grouse Mountain Skyride Base
pois.intro: Grouse Mountain is one of the North Shore Mountains of the Pacific Ranges in the District Municipality of North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. With a maximum elevation of over 1,200 m at its peak, the mountain is the site of an alpine ski area, Grouse Mountain Resort, which overlooks Metro Vancouver and has four chairlifts servicing 33 runs.

pois.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
pois.intro: Queen Elizabeth Park is a 130-acre municipal park located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is located on top of Little Mountain approximately 125 metres above sea level and is the location of former basalt quarries dug in the beginning of the twentieth century to provide materials for roads in the city.

pois.name: Vancouver Aquarium
pois.intro: The Vancouver Aquarium is a public aquarium located in Stanley Park in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. In addition to being a major tourist attraction for Vancouver, the aquarium is a centre for marine research, ocean literacy education, climate activism, conservation and marine animal rehabilitation.

pois.name: Vancouver Maritime Museum
pois.openingHours: Su-Sa 10:00-17:00; Sep-May: Mo off; Sep-May: Su 12:00-17:00
pois.intro: The Vancouver Maritime Museum is a maritime museum devoted to presenting the maritime history of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, and the Canadian Arctic. Opened in 1959 as a Vancouver centennial project, it is located within Vanier Park just west of False Creek on the Vancouver waterfront.

pois.name: Ben Franklin
pois.intro: The Ben Franklin mesoscaphe, also known as the Grumman/Piccard PX-15, is a crewed underwater submersible, built in 1968. It was the brainchild of explorer and inventor Jacques Piccard.

pois.name: Hillcrest Park
pois.intro: Hillcrest Park is located in the Riley Park neighbourhood of Vancouver, British Columbia. It is located immediately north of Queen Elizabeth Park and west of Riley Park.

pois.name: BC Sports Hall of Fame and Museum
pois.intro: The BC Sports Hall of Fame is a museum located in the BC Place stadium, at Gate A, the main entrance to the stadium, in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It collects, preserves, studies and interprets materials that relate to British Columbia's sport history, and allows researchers, writers, media members and sport historians to gain access to and appreciate BC's sporting heritage.

pois.name: Science World
pois.intro: Science World is a science centre run by a not-for-profit organization called ASTC Science World Society in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is located at the eastern end of False Creek and features many permanent interactive exhibits and displays, as well as areas with varying topics throughout the years.

pois.name: Museum of Vancouver
pois.intro: The Museum of Vancouver is a civic history museum located in Vanier Park, Vancouver, British Columbia. MOV is the largest urban museum in Canada and the oldest museum in Vancouver.

pois.name: Vancouver Police Museum
pois.intro: The Vancouver Police Museum & Archives opened to commemorate the centennial of the Vancouver Police Department and the City of Vancouver, British Columbia in 1986.

pois.name: Gallery Gachet
pois.intro: Gachet Gallery is an artist-run art gallery in the Downtown Eastside neighborhood of Vancouver. It is named after Paul Gachet, the physician of Vincent van Gogh.

pois.name: H. R. MacMillan Space Centre
pois.intro: The H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, is an astronomy museum located at Vanier Park in Vancouver, British Columbia. The museum was opened on October 28, 1968, containing a Planetarium Star Theatre.

pois.name: Roedde House Museum
pois.intro: The Roedde House Museum is a late-Victorian home located at 1415 Barclay Street in Vancouver, Canada. It was the home of Gustav Roedde and his family.

pois.name: The Polygon Gallery
pois.intro: The Polygon Gallery is an art gallery in North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is the largest non-profit photographic gallery in Western Canada and has operated since 1981.

pois.name: Orpheum
pois.intro: The Orpheum is a theatre and music venue in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Along with the Queen Elizabeth Theatre, the Vancouver Playhouse, and the Annex, it is part of the Vancouver Civic Theatres group of live performance venues.

pois.name: Bill Reid Gallery of Northwest Coast Art
pois.description: An art gallery with Bill Reid's art. Entrance has a fee. Gift shop is free to access.

pois.name: Centre of International Contemporary Art Vancouver
Nine O'Clock Gun
pois.intro: The 9 O'Clock Gun is a cannon located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, that is ordinarily fired daily at 21:00 PT.

pois.name: St. Lawrence Restaurant
pois.intro: St. Lawrence is a French-Canadian restaurant in the Japantown neighbourhood of Vancouver, British Columbia.

pois.name: Moltaqa
pois.intro: Moltaqa is a Moroccan restaurant in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

pois.name: Kissa Tanto
pois.intro: Kissa Tanto is an Italian-Japanese fusion restaurant in the Chinatown neighborhood of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The 80-seat restaurant, which opened in June 2016, is on the second floor of 263 E Pender St.

pois.name: Phnom Penh Restaurant
pois.intro: Phnom Penh is a restaurant located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It serves Vietnamese and Cambodian cuisine.

pois.name: Elisa
pois.intro: Elisa is a steakhouse in Yaletown, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Toptable Group opened the restaurant in 2018.

pois.name: Seaport City Seafood Restaurant
pois.intro: Seaport City Seafood is a Chinese restaurant in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

pois.name: Steamworks
pois.intro: The Steamworks Brewing Company is a Canadian microbrewery based in Burnaby, British Columbia. Founded in 1995, Steamworks was originally based out of the Gastown brewpub located in the city of Vancouver.

pois.name: Salmon n' Bannock
pois.intro: Salmon n' Bannock is a restaurant in the Fairview neighbourhood in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, situated on the Broadway thoroughfare. First opening in 2010, it expanded in 2022 to a second location in the Vancouver International Airport dubbed Salmon n' Bannock On The Fly.

pois.name: CF Pacific Centre
pois.intro: Pacific Centre is a shopping mall located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is owned by Cadillac Fairview, the Ontario Pension Board, and the Workplace Safety and Insurance Board, and is managed by Cadillac Fairview.

pois.name: Lonsdale Quay Market
pois.intro: Lonsdale Quay Market is a major public market and tourist destination located in the city of North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The market is located at the foot of Lonsdale Avenue and is adjacent to the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus terminal and transit exchange that serves Metro Vancouver's North Shore municipalities.

pois.name: Spartacus Books
pois.description: Spartacus Books is a nonprofit, volunteer-run bookstore and resource centre. The store has been run collectively for over 40 years.
pois.intro: Spartacus Books is a non-profit, volunteer and collectively run bookstore and resource centre in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It was founded in 1973.

pois.name: Park Royal Shopping Centre
pois.intro: Park Royal Shopping Centre, also known as simply Park Royal, opened in 1950, is a shopping mall located in West Vancouver and X̱wemelch'stn, British Columbia, Canada. Park Royal was Canada's first covered shopping mall.

pois.name: Douglas Reynolds Gallery
pois.intro: Douglas Reynolds Gallery[1] specializes in world renowned Indigenous Northwest Coast art. Working directly with a variety of artists, the gallery represents cultural groups spanning from the Haida and Tlingit in Northern British Columbia, to the Coast Salish in the Vancouver area and Northern Washington state.

pois.name: Sinclair Centre
pois.intro: Sinclair Centre is an upscale shopping mall in Downtown Vancouver, British Columbia. It is located at 757 West Hastings Street between Granville and Howe streets by the Waterfront Station.

pois.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
pois.openingHours: Sep Mo[1] +1 day-Oct 31: Mo-Su 09:00-17:00; Nov-Dec: Mo-Su 10:00-14:00; Dec 25 off
pois.intro: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a botanical garden in Vancouver, British Columbia, in the Shaughnessy neighborhood. It is located at the northwest corner of 37th Avenue and Oak Street.

pois.name: Victory Square
pois.intro: Victory Square is a park in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The square is bordered by West Hastings Street to the northeast, West Pender Street to the southwest, Cambie Street to the southeast, and Hamilton Street to the northwest.

pois.name: Bloedel Floral Conservatory
pois.openingHours: Jan-Feb: Mo-Su 10:00-16:00; Mar-Apr: Mo-Su 10:00-18:00; May 01-Sep Mo[1] +1 day: Mo-Su 10:00-19:00; Sep Mo[1] +1 day-Oct 31: Mo-Su 10:00-17:00; Nov-Dec Mo-Su 10:00-16:00; Dec 25 off
pois.intro: The Bloedel Conservatory is a domed conservatory and aviary located at the top of Queen Elizabeth Park in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Opened in 1969, it was funded through a major donation from the Bloedel Foundation alongside contributions from Vancouver City Council and the Vancouver Park Board.

pois.name: Kitsilano Beach
pois.intro: Kitsilano Beach is a beach on English Bay in the Kitsilano neighborhood of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It is one of the most popular beaches in the city.

pois.name: Robson Square
pois.intro: Robson Square is a landmark civic centre and public plaza, located in Downtown Vancouver, British Columbia. It is the site of the Provincial Law Courts, UBC Robson Square, government office buildings, and public space connecting the newer development to the Vancouver Art Gallery.

pois.name: Oppenheimer Park
pois.intro: Oppenheimer Park is a park located in the historic Japantown in the Downtown Eastside, Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

pois.name: Second Beach
pois.intro: Second Beach is located at Stanley Park in Vancouver, British Columbia. The beach features a pool, which was first completed in 1932.

pois.name: Lunch Lady
pois.intro: Lunch Lady is a Vietnamese restaurant in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It has received Bib Gourmand status.
